role: SUPERSEDED by team-lead ruling 2026-08-24: esp-soc-2's system-regmap.json is a strict superset (adds PERIP_CLK_EN0/PERIP_RST_EN0 clock gating) and pins an IDF tag rather than master - better on both counts, per esp-soc's own assessment. Kept, not deleted, so the original two-register verification trail below stays auditable.
source: ESP-IDF master as read 2026-08-24: components/soc/esp32c3/register/soc/system_reg.h (offsets); components/esp_hal_clock/esp32c3/include/hal/clk_tree_ll.h and components/esp_hw_support/port/esp32c3/rtc_clk.c (semantics). Register-name facts elected under the headers' MIT option (SPDX Apache-2.0 OR MIT)
verified: 2026-08-24 offsets quoted from system_reg.h; semantics from clk_tree_ll.h as read - a grep of its 789 lines found zero busy-wait loops, and the CPU/SoC clock switch has no readiness handshake on the C3: rtc_clk.c uses fixed esp_rom_delay_us waits (lines 129, 150). Only the two registers the clock path actually touches are listed; everything else in the block falls to the unknown-offset default and the accounting report. The C3 TRM PDF was not consulted

fields.name: ALL
fields.why: CPUPERIOD_SEL / PLL_FREQ_SEL written by clk_ll_cpu_set_freq_mhz_from_pll (clk_tree_ll.h:273) when esp_clk_init raises the CPU to 160 MHz; read back by rtc_clk_cpu_freq_get_config - reads-zero would misreport the current frequency, not hang

fields.name: ALL
fields.why: SOC_CLK_SEL (XTAL/PLL/RC_FAST) and PRE_DIV_CNT (clk_tree_ll.h:415); the switch takes effect immediately with no SWS-style mirror to poll - the C3 differs from STM32 here, and modelling it as plain storage is the verified contract, not a shortcut
